title: Grade 8 INTEGRATED SCIENCE — Elements and Compounds (Screen Drama)
body:
EPISODE PACKAGE
====

EPISODE TITLE: THE LABEL THAT LIED
SUBJECT / TOPIC: INTEGRATED SCIENCE / Elements and Compounds
GRADE: Grade 8 JSS
AGE RATING: 10+ (student-safe)
DURATION: 8 minutes
VISUAL STYLE: naturalistic live-action look with clear prop inserts (or 2D/3D cartoon adaptation of the same blocking)

LEARNING TIE-IN: Nzuri wants to advise Auntie Halima correctly using element and compound knowledge

LOGLINE: A young shop helper misreads chemical names on salt and toothpaste labels and almost mixes the wrong advice for a customer.

WORLD & CAST
----
• Setting / era: INT./EXT. neighbourhood duka and kitchen, present-day Kenya
• NZURI: 16, shop helper, curious, quick to guess. Costume: school-clean blouse, apron.
• BIKE: duka owner, patient, precise. Costume: checked shirt, calculator in pocket.
• AUNTIE HALIMA: customer buying salt and toothpaste. Costume: kitenge, handbag.

SCREENPLAY
----

SCENE 1 — EXT./INT. OPENING LOCATION — DAY
----
ACTION: NZURI enters the world of the story with a clear goal: Nzuri wants to advise Auntie Halima correctly using element and compound knowledge. Camera follows hands and faces, not a chalkboard.

NZURI
If I can just get this right today, everything else will fall into place.

BIKE
Then stop guessing. Show me what you think is happening.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Wide establishing → medium two-shot. Ambient authentic location SFX. Soft hopeful underscore.

SCENE 2 — SAME / NEARBY — DAY
----
ACTION: Obstacle appears. Stakes rise. Props related to the science idea are handled as real objects, not lecture aids.

NZURI
It looks simple. Watch me do it the usual way.

AUNTIE HALIMA
If you are wrong, we lose time — and maybe more than time.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Close-ups on props and worried eyes. Tension riser.

NZURI
If we ignore the detail, we will repeat the same mistake under pressure.

BIKE
Then name the detail out loud while you do the action — teaching by doing, not by speech notes.

SCENE 3 — CONFRONTATION — DAY
----
ACTION: WRONG WAY: She treats NaCl as an element and writes CA for calcium. The problem worsens. Meaning stays in action and argument — characters never read notes aloud.

NZURI
See? I did what everyone does.

BIKE
And it got worse. That means your idea about it is incomplete.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Handheld urgency. Cut to the failed result.

SCENE 4 — DISCOVERY — DAY/NIGHT
----
ACTION: A clue appears through action — a label, a measurement, a safer method, a remembered rule spoken as dialogue while doing.

BIKE
Look at what actually changed. Name it properly.

NZURI
Wait… if that is true, then I was measuring the wrong thing.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Insert shots of evidence. Music shifts from tension to curiosity.

NZURI
If we ignore the detail, we will repeat the same mistake under pressure.

BIKE
Then name the detail out loud while you do the action — teaching by doing, not by speech notes.

SCENE 5 — SECOND ATTEMPT — DAY
----
ACTION: RIGHT WAY: She uses capitalization rules and Latin roots to correct the labels. Characters perform the corrected action step by step.

NZURI
This time we follow the rule, not the rumour.

AUNTIE HALIMA
I can see the difference already.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Cleaner framed shots; success micro-beats.

SCENE 6 — COMPLICATION — DAY
----
ACTION: A new obstacle or time pressure forces them to apply the idea again, proving it was not luck.

AUNTIE HALIMA
We are not done. Another problem just arrived.

BIKE
Same science. Fresh situation. Go.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Parallel cut or ticking clock motif without graphic peril.

NZURI
If we ignore the detail, we will repeat the same mistake under pressure.

BIKE
Then name the detail out loud while you do the action — teaching by doing, not by speech notes.

SCENE 7 — RESOLUTION — DAY
----
ACTION: Payoff: goal achieved. Characters show the result; still no voice-over lecture.

NZURI
It worked because we used the idea correctly — not because we pushed harder the same wrong way.

BIKE
Say the reason in your own words before we pack up.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Warm wider shot; relieved faces; result hero insert.

SCENE 8 — BUTTON — DAY
----
ACTION: Final acted beat tying emotion to the learning without reading notes aloud.

AUNTIE HALIMA
Next time someone guesses, we will ask for the reason.

NZURI
And we will check the evidence first.

CAMERA / SFX / MUSIC: Slow push-in; music resolves.

NZURI
If we ignore the detail, we will repeat the same mistake under pressure.

BIKE
Then name the detail out loud while you do the action — teaching by doing, not by speech notes.

BOOKENDS
----
• COLD OPEN (max 10s): Quick hook image of the failed first attempt — then cut to title THE LABEL THAT LIED.
• CLOSING REFLECTION CARD (max 10s): On-screen question — Why must chemical symbols follow capitalization rules? Answer must match lesson solutions (Q1/A1 from symbols pages — first letter capital, second lowercase).

CAPTIONS
----
NZURI: If I can just get this right today, everything else will fall into place.
BIKE: Then stop guessing. Show me what you think is happening.
NZURI: It looks simple. Watch me do it the usual way.
AUNTIE HALIMA: If you are wrong, we lose time — and maybe more than time.
NZURI: See? I did what everyone does.
BIKE: And it got worse. That means your idea about it is incomplete.
BIKE: Look at what actually changed. Name it properly.
NZURI: Wait… if that is true, then I was measuring the wrong thing.
NZURI: This time we follow the rule, not the rumour.
AUNTIE HALIMA: I can see the difference already.
AUNTIE HALIMA: We are not done. Another problem just arrived.
BIKE: Same science. Fresh situation. Go.
NZURI: It worked because we used the idea correctly — not because we pushed harder the same wrong way.
BIKE: Say the reason in your own words before we pack up.
AUNTIE HALIMA: Next time someone guesses, we will ask for the reason.
NZURI: And we will check the evidence first.

ASSET LIST
----
• Characters: NZURI, BIKE, AUNTIE HALIMA
• Costumes: as listed above
• Locations: INT./EXT. neighbourhood duka and kitchen, present-day Kenya
• Props: topic-authentic objects for Elements and Compounds
• Key shots: failed attempt insert, evidence insert, successful payoff insert

Study pages available for fidelity: 20
DRAMA NOTE: No voice-over of lesson notes. Meaning travels through action and in-character dialogue.
